technical_and_design_decisions: For U2 (uber-jar in HDFS): Use the Hadoop filesystem API (HDFS client) to upload the uber-jar; build tool (Gradle/Maven) will produce a fat jar including all dependencies.
For U3 (WebSocket sink): Implement a Spring Integration WebSocket outbound channel adapter as the sink; leverage Spring's WebSocket support (e.g., SockJS, STOMP).
For U4 (CI research): Evaluate npm-cache as a caching layer for npm dependencies within the CI pipeline; design a script to integrate it with the existing build tool.

For U5 (EC2 CI improvements): Enable distributed JVM test execution by configuring Gradle's 'maxParallelForks' and switching from the artifactory Gradle task to direct './gradlew' invocation; disable embedded Hadoop for tests.
For U6 (WARN logs & Sonar): Use static analysis tools (PMD, SonarQube) to identify violations; update code to suppress warnings and configure Sonar notifications for committers.
For U7 (Windows CI setup): Use Bamboo's agent capabilities to run on Windows; install prerequisite services (Redis, RabbitMQ) via PowerShell; configure the build plan to trigger on commit.
For U8 (shared jar location): Implement a classloader mechanism in the custom module system to load shared jars from the 'xd/lib' directory while allowing version-specific bundling in modules.
Overall: All development is in Java 17+ using Spring Framework 6.0, Gradle for build, and Spring Cloud Data Flow as the underlying platform.
assumptions: The existing codebase is based on Spring XD / Spring Cloud Data Flow.
The developer has full access to the source code repository and a working development environment.
HDFS is available and the necessary Hadoop client libraries are already part of the project dependencies.
CI infrastructure (Bamboo, Windows agents) is already provisioned or can be created with minimal effort.
Each user story includes its own unit and integration testing, as well as documentation updates where required.
Effort estimates are for a single experienced developer working full-time; no overhead for meetings or non-development tasks.
The 'npm-cache' tool mentioned in U4 is compatible with the project's build pipeline.
The WebSocket sink in U3 is a new module that will be added to the existing set of sinks.
The shared jar location (U8) is a configuration change and does not require a major refactoring of the classloader.

activities.activity_description: Create or update documentation describing recommended standards and patterns for building custom modules, including code examples and best practices.

activities.activity_name: Host custom module as uber-jar in HDFS
activities.activity_description: Implement build logic to create an uber-jar (fat jar) and a deployment mechanism to upload it to HDFS. Ensure newly arriving containers can download and use the jar.
Design and develop a new WebSocket sink component using Spring Framework's WebSocket support, enabling full-duplex communication over a single TCP connection.

activities.activity_name: Research CI options for build stability
activities.activity_description: Evaluate npm-cache and other caching strategies to reduce dependency download times; document findings and propose an implementation plan.
Modify CI configuration to enable distributed JVM tests, switch to direct './gradlew' command, disable embedded Hadoop, and set maxParallelForks to improve test performance.

activities.activity_name: Investigate and fix WARN logs and Sonar violations
activities.activity_description: Analyze increased WARN logs, fix PMD/Sonar violations in the codebase, and configure Sonar notifications to alert the committer.
Configure Bamboo to run integration tests on Windows agents: install PowerShell, set up Redis and RabbitMQ services, and create a commit-triggered build plan.
Add support for a shared directory ('xd/lib') for jars needed by multiple custom modules, and update classloader logic to handle version conflicts via bundling.
